notes:
Nyxen 1.13.0 - glossy buddies, DJ decks, a cinema, building from above

Nyxen Space (beta): everyone is a glossy buddy now, like the old messenger
icon - a droplet of a body on two legs, a round head floating just above it,
a shine, a glow and an outline. Any colour; glossy, jelly, two-tone, chrome or
oil-slick. The sky is a soft grey.

DJ decks: walk up, press E and paste any song link - YouTube, Spotify, Apple
Music, SoundCloud - or type a song. Everyone in the space hears it in time,
louder near the decks, and the records spin. Queue, skip and stop. The lobby
has a set.

Screens: a cinema screen to build, as well as the TV. Both show whoever shares
their screen, and E watches them. When you walk up to a couch, a door, a
screen or the decks, it says what E will do.

Building: you see the real piece you are about to place, in its colour. Hold
and drag to draw walls, rooms and floors, with the size shown as you go, and
drag Erase over an area to clear it. Move picks anything up - the TV, the
couch - to put it somewhere else. Tab gives a top view to build like a city
builder: left click builds (drag for a line of road), right click removes,
right-drag turns and the wheel zooms. New roof slopes and round columns, and
the blocks have real texture: bricks with mortar, planks, tiles, cobbles.

Nyxen 1.12.0 - Nyxen in the tray, 3D that always opens, reopening fixed

Nyxen lives in the tray now - the icons by the clock. Click it to open Nyxen.
Right-click it for your status, the song playing on your PC (pause, next,
previous), muting or leaving the call you are in, starting a game you played
lately, a screenshot, Messages, the live map, the Space, checking for updates,
starting with Windows, and Quit.

Closing the window keeps Nyxen running in the tray, like Discord, so messages
and calls still reach you. Switch that off in Settings or in the tray menu.

Opening Nyxen always works again. If an earlier copy got stuck - it happened
after Avast's CyberCapture closed Nyxen - the new one clears it and starts,
instead of doing nothing.

3D opens even when the graphics card cannot be used (while Avast is checking
Nyxen, for example): the live map in blocks and the Space draw on the
processor instead of failing with "Error creating WebGL context".

Also fixed: the arrows on the Advanced sections in Settings, and Bluetooth
"AG Audio" headsets are recognised as hands-free again.

Nyxen 1.11.0 - the Space moves into Social, city building, a smooth 3D map

The 3D Minecraft map is smooth now. It had a bug that re-read your world and
rebuilt all of it every second or two while you played - that was the lag. On
top of fixing it, the terrain is built in the background (the app never
freezes while it loads), only the part on screen is drawn, and nothing at all
is drawn while it sits still. Same blocks, same quality - checked face by face.

2D or 3D, one click: the live map has a 2D | 3D switch that is always there,
also in full screen, and the M key flips it. Switching is instant, and Nyxen
remembers which one you like and opens it that way next time you play.

Nyxen Space (beta) is now a tab in Social. The figures are taller and real
chrome, and you can dress yours: any colour, mirror, satin, oil-slick or
two-tone, height, build, head, face and a hat. Chat pops up as a bubble over
whoever is talking. The white world has its grid floor back and a softer,
dimmer light; glass is less see-through.

Build like a city builder: whole walls, rooms and floors in one drag, windows,
stairs, fences, roads and crosswalks, lamps, traffic lights, cars, benches,
trees - and ready-made houses, shops, office towers, apartments, parks and
parking lots. Paint, pick, undo and redo. Make your own spaces, light or dark.

Nyxen 1.10.0 - Minecraft in 3D blocks, the 3D Space (beta), a natural voice

Minecraft live map in real 3D blocks: press 3D on the live map and your world
appears as cubes - read from the save on your PC, textured with your game's own
block pictures (or the Clean model look), with trees, water, snow, houses, your
friends and your waypoints on it, lit for the time of day. "Explore a world in
3D" works with the game closed, in the Overworld, the Nether and the End.

Nyxen Space (beta): a white 3D world for you and your friends. Walk around as a
puffy chrome figure with a floating head in the chrome colour you pick, talk
(people sound quieter the further away they are), sit on the couch, watch
whoever shares their screen on the TV, chat, and build together - blocks and
furniture - Minecraft-style. Open it from Social > Home. It can be switched off
in Settings > Beta.

A natural voice for the assistant: one download from Settings > AI > Voice and
it speaks like a person instead of a robot. It runs on your PC - no key,
nothing sent anywhere.

Spotify and Apple Music: the song shows up the moment it changes (it used to
take up to 10-20 seconds) and with its cover - Nyxen now takes the picture
straight from the player, so it works even for songs no music store knows, and
your friends see it too.

Social > Home is a real home now: you, your game and your song at the top, the
feed, and who is online, live rooms, who is playing what and people you may know
beside it. Layouts: the Dock's tab names no longer sit on top of the icons,
Hub shows your song with its cover and controls, and Couch is bigger for a TV.

Nyxen 1.9.1 - Minecraft online, tested for real

Play online was run for real in Minecraft 1.21.1 (on a hidden desktop) and two
problems turned up and are fixed. On PCs whose antivirus scans secure
connections (Avast does), Minecraft's Java refused them, so e4mc could never
get a relay; turning Play online on for a pack now tells that pack's Java to use
Windows' certificates, and turning it off puts your Java settings back exactly.
And Nyxen now reads the world's address only from e4mc's own "hosted on
domain" message. Result: the world went online and answered from the internet
with its name, version and player count.

Nyxen 1.9.0 - easier to find your way, three more layouts, and a better you

Help: the new ? button at the top (or F1) explains everything Nyxen does in
plain words, with a search and a Take me there button on each answer. And a
short tour - Show me around - points out each part of the app. New users are
offered it once.

Three more layouts, for ten in all (Settings > Themes): Hub puts your friends,
what they are playing and the live rooms in a column on the right; Zen hides
everything but the page, with the menu one button away; Couch is big and
simple, for a TV and a controller.

Your profile (Social > You) is rebuilt: your banner and ring, what you are
playing and listening to right now, your stats, and Finish your profile, which
shows what is missing and takes you straight to it.

Retro games online now just work: tested for real with two RetroArch
copies. RetroArch asks the joining player for the password, so Nyxen types it
for them; it joins the newest room (not a closed one still listed); your own
RetroArch settings are no longer changed by an online session; and the game
does not pause for both players when one of you clicks away.

Nyxen 1.8.1 - smooth again

1.7.1 moved everyone onto drawing with the processor to stop black windows.
It worked, but it made Nyxen scroll at about 17 frames a second and use a
whole CPU core while doing nothing. Nyxen is back on the graphics card - now
scrolling as fast as your screen can show - and it still switches to safe
drawing by itself if the graphics card's process ever fails, so the black
window does not come back.

Nyxen also uses almost nothing while it sits there: animated rings, name
effects and the like now play while you are using the window and settle a few
seconds after you stop (or as soon as you are in a game), instead of redrawing
the screen forever. Measured on the same window: a full core at rest before,
about 2% now.

Nyxen 1.8.0 - play together online, a smarter library, and more Eclipse

Minecraft online with friends: in Minecraft > Play together > Play online,
switch it on for a pack (Nyxen adds the e4mc mod from Modrinth, and removes it
again when you switch it off). Then open your world and press Esc > Open to
LAN - Nyxen shows the address it gets, with no port forwarding, and Invite
friends sends it to them. They get a card in their chat, and Join starts
their own matching pack straight into your world.

Retro games online: every game on the Retro shelf has an Online button.
RetroArch starts it as the host through libretro's relay, with a password only
your friends get, and Nyxen sends them the invite. Their Join finds the same
game in their own ROM folders - by name, or by checksum if they named it
differently - and the right core, and connects them to you.

Library: favourites, hidden games, and your own collections (Co-op nights,
Finish these...), a Continue playing row with the games you played last, and
a menu on every game - Steam store page, SteamDB, PCGamingWiki, mods, guides,
how much space it takes, open its folder, or uninstall it through Steam.

Nyxen Eclipse: send a message with confetti, hearts, fireworks, snow or stars
that both of you see; six more name effects (Neon, Glitch, Gold, Aurora,
Matrix, Sparkle); animated profile card themes; screen share at 60 fps; and
five ringtones to choose from.

Also: menus never run off the bottom of the window any more.

Nyxen 1.7.2 - your choices stay chosen

Nyxen now remembers everything you set in the app between restarts - the
interface style (Dock, Top bar, Glass...), your accent colour, font and panel
transparency, the notification and message-sound switches, the live map's
look, how you sort your mods and more. Before, the window started with a
clean slate each time and some of these quietly went back to the defaults.

The website's download box shows the right version again.

Nyxen 1.7.1 - no more black window, lighter on your PC, and real layouts

Stability: when the graphics side of the window failed, Nyxen used to be left
as a black window (or just closed). Now it notices and recovers by itself - a
crashed page reloads, a graphics failure switches Nyxen to safe drawing and
reopens the window in a couple of seconds, and a window whose page never
loads is reloaded and then reopened. Only one Nyxen runs at a time: opening
it again brings the running one to the front. And Nyxen now keeps a small
log (in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Nyxen\logs), so a problem can actually be traced.

Lighter: everyone starts on safe drawing (on the processor, not the graphics
card), which is what was tied to black windows and PC freezes here. Settings >
Advanced switches the graphics card back on, and says when and why it was
switched off. Animated backgrounds and effects now pause while Nyxen is behind
a game or another window, so they never compete with what you are playing.

Interface styles now change the layout, not just the corners: Studio (a slim
icon rail), Fluent (big page titles, centred), Glass (a floating sidebar and
title bar), Top bar (navigation across the top), Dock (no sidebar - a dock at
the bottom that magnifies, like a Mac) and Console (text navigation on the
right). Settings > Themes.

Nyxen 1.7.0 - new chats, rooms and profiles, a full-screen live map, and Eclipse trials

Chats: rebuilt like a real messenger - replies, reactions, edits and deletes,
"typing..." and "Seen", grouped bubbles and day separators, search and pinned
conversations. Windows tells you about a new message or an incoming call
while Nyxen is in the background, with a ringtone for calls. In a call you can
share your screen (it says LIVE next to your name) and start music together -
you both hear the same song in step while you talk.

Rooms: a clearer layout - the room list on the left, the room on the right,
with Chat, Voice and screen, Music, Game nights, Mods and Members as tabs.
Anyone in the room can DJ.

Profiles and friends: a new profile card with your banner and ring, and what
you are doing right now - the game (Steam, Roblox, Minecraft, RetroArch) and
how long for, and the song, with whether it is on Spotify or Apple Music.
Friends show as cards grouped into In a game, Online and Offline, with
Message and Call one click away.

Minecraft live map in full screen: press F (or the new button) and the map
fills the screen with everything around it - the server and who is on it,
the players near you with a direction arrow, who is in your call and who is
talking, the room's music with controls, your clock and the game's time of
day, a compass, waypoints, and in single-player your hotbar, health, food,
experience and whole inventory (E). Seven map looks: Classic, Vivid,
Parchment, Blueprint, Noir, Thermal and Night vision.

Worth a look, on Home: games free to keep right now (Epic Games Store and
more), the best Steam deals, and the latest patch notes for the games you
play.

Mods: filter, sort and switch every mod on or off at once; remove a mod
without losing it (put it back any time); back up the whole mod folder and
restore it later.

Interface styles: Studio, Fluent, Glass, Dense and Console change the shape
of everything - corners, surfaces, titles and spacing - on top of any theme.

Nyxen Eclipse: 1, 3, 6 or 12 months (the longer, the cheaper), and a 7-day
free trial. The trial needs a credit or debit card at checkout; nothing is
charged for 7 days and cancelling before then costs nothing.

Also: break reminders after long sessions (off unless you switch them on,
in Settings), Windows notifications and message sounds can be switched off
in Settings, and name effects now show on comments too.

Nyxen 1.6.1 - updates that install themselves, and music that plays

Updates: new versions now download quietly in the background. When one is
ready the top bar says "Restart to update" - or just close Nyxen and it
installs on the way out. After updating, "What's new" shows once.

Room music: when a song's YouTube upload is blocked outside YouTube ("This
video is unavailable"), Nyxen finds another upload that plays - and if the
label blocks it everywhere, plays it from SoundCloud instead, in step for
the whole room. You can add songs by name now, or paste a Spotify, Apple
Music or SoundCloud link. Anyone in the room's call can DJ; the owner can
lock it to one person. Music asks YouTube for HD audio, drops to half
volume (not a quarter) while someone talks, and stays tighter in sync.
If your headphones switch to muffled hands-free mode in a call, Nyxen tells
you how to keep them in stereo.

Full screen fits every window size: the music player sizes itself to the
window, and a shared screen's Full screen now fills your whole monitor.

Name effects now show on every name - the sidebar, the top bar, calls, room
chat, the feed and leaderboards - and room chat uses the sender's bubble.

The assistant is Nyxen AI and says so.

Nyxen 1.6.0 - a live Minecraft map, lyrics, mods for every game, and Eclipse v2

Playing a game starts it: choose a game at the top and Steam launches it -
Nyxen used to only load it, and a loaded game could even stop Steam from
starting it. Shift+click, or the trophy, still just reads its achievements.

Minecraft live map: switch it on for any pack - Fabric, Forge, NeoForge or
Quilt, from 1.7.10 to the newest versions - and Nyxen adds JourneyMap with
its web map (and Fabric API if the pack needs it). While you play, the Live
map tab shows your world, your coordinates, biome and facing, the players
around you with their heads, and the server with its icon and player count.
Switching it off removes exactly what was added.

Music: a full-screen player in the Apple Music style, with the cover large,
the artwork melted into a moving background and the lyrics scrolling in time
with the song. The DJ can tap a line to jump there. Or switch Lyrics on to
see the current line under the song.

Mods for any installed game - pick it at the top of Mods, no loading needed.
Nexus Mods joins Thunderstore, GameBanana, Modrinth and the Workshop: browse
and search there, download on Nexus's page, and Nyxen installs the file the
moment it lands in your Downloads (zip, 7z and rar).

Eclipse v2: twenty animated rings - fire, neon, rainbow, sakura, glitch,
galaxy and more - or design your own with your colours, movement, speed and
thickness. New: name effects, chat bubble styles and a moving profile banner.

Themes: every animated theme redrawn with far more detail - parallax stars
and shooting stars, auroras made of curtains, rain with lightning and
splashes, a circuit grid - plus four new ones: Cherry blossom, Fireflies,
Spiral galaxy and Synthwave.

Achievements show their real pictures without a Steam key, and the game's
portrait when there is none. Your rarest achievements now fill in for
keyless accounts too. Library art comes from Steam's own copy on your PC,
so newer games no longer show initials.

Fixed: at the very bottom of a long page the sidebar slid up and left a
black strip.

Nyxen 1.5.0 - game nights, a soundboard, and your week

Game nights in rooms: pick a time and a game, and everyone in the room is
told. Friends answer "I'm in" or "Can't make it", you see who is coming, and
whoever is in gets a reminder ten minutes before it starts - in their own
time zone.

A soundboard in calls, for Eclipse members: add up to twelve clips of your
own, ten seconds each, and play them into the call. Everyone hears them,
every clip is played at the same level so nobody gets blasted, and nothing
is uploaded - the clips stay on your PC.

Your week, on Home: the last seven days in numbers - time played, games, the
days you played, achievements and your most played game - and one click has
the AI write it up, with a suggestion for next week.

Nyxen 1.4.0 - every theme, with depth

Every theme now lights the app from its own colours: a soft glow from two
corners, a faint grain so dark screens stop looking like flat fill, card
edges that catch the light, glowing icon tiles on card titles, richer
buttons and numbers, and a badge for the section you are in beside its title.
None of it animates continuously, and graphics-safe mode turns the heavier
parts off.

Themes has its own gallery at the top of Settings: every theme drawn as a
miniature of Nyxen in its own colours, grouped, one click to switch.

Nyxen 1.3.0 - Eclipse, priced, and an AI that writes properly

Nyxen Eclipse is now $8.59 a month, or $69.99 a year - $5.83 a month, 32%
less, and yearly members get the gold ring. A membership lasts a month or a
year from when it is given, a renewal adds on to the time left, and when it
ends the ring and your theme are kept for when you come back. Whoever runs
your Nyxen has Eclipse themselves, and can give a month or a year to a friend
or make codes. The website has the plans too.

Your ring works: the decorations and the accent colour save to your profile,
and anyone can try them on first to see how they look.

AI answers read like writing, not code: no more ** and # in the text. Lists
are real lists, labels are bold, titles stand out - in the chat and
everywhere else an answer appears.

Nyxen 1.2.2 - updates that really update

A taskbar pin made from an older copy of Nyxen kept opening that old copy
after every update, so an update could look as if it had never happened.
Installing or updating now points a Nyxen pin on your taskbar at the copy it
just installed (other pins are never touched). Updates from inside the app
also no longer flash the setup's splash screen over whatever you are playing.

Nyxen 1.2.1 - no more error box over your game

Closing Nyxen while a game was running could leave a "Failed to execute
script 'app'" box with a Python traceback on screen. It came from the small
background helper Nyxen starts to talk to Steam: it tried to answer an app
that had already closed. It now stops quietly - and always tells Steam the
game session is over on the way out, so Steam does not think a game is still
running after you closed it.

Nyxen 1.2.0 - a new look, and the things that were promised

A reworked interface. The sidebar runs the full height of the window with one
highlight that slides to where you go, and folds down to icons if you want the
room. The top bar says where you are and holds what you reach for from
anywhere: search, the game you are working with, notifications and your
account. Screens slide in from the direction you moved, every screen has one
line saying what it is for, and messages stack instead of replacing each other.

Ctrl+K finds anything - every screen, every setting, every action and every
game in your library. The bell keeps notifications that arrived while you were
in a game. New to Nyxen? A short welcome sets up your account, Steam and a
look, and a Getting started list on Home keeps the first steps in reach.

Nyxen Eclipse, the membership: a ring on your picture everywhere, your own
picture or animated GIF as a theme, a voice changer in calls (deep, chipmunk,
robot, radio, demon, cave and more, with a pitch slider, switchable mid-call),
avatar decorations and a profile accent colour. Nothing is charged in the app:
a membership comes from whoever runs your Nyxen, directly or with a code.

The AI works with no key and no setup - Nyxen Free AI answers when you have no
Ollama and no key of your own, and it answers about the game you name even if
another one is loaded.

Forgot your password? Every account now has a recovery key that works from any
PC. Existing accounts can make one in Social - You - Account.

Watch an achievement and hear the moment a friend unlocks it - achievements in
your showcase are watched for you. "What can we play?" on a friend shows the
games you both have, co-op and multiplayer first, and the AI can pick one.
Share cards turn your Wrapped or your profile into a picture to post anywhere.
Pick your own accent colour, panel transparency and font, on top of any theme.

Fixed: popovers such as Add a friend opened in the wrong place once the page
had scrolled; twenty panels in the Toolkit, Retro and Audio had their text
against the edge; several borders were missing; light themes drew dark panels;
the Social tab kept describing Home.

The Minecraft tab shows your modpacks as their own artwork - the pictures
your launcher already has, animated GIFs included - with a Change picture
button on each, and a list view if you prefer rows. Selecting one marks it
the way the rest of Nyxen marks a selection.

Five more neutral themes: Ash, Stone, Ink, Fog and Sand. And a theme of your
own - any picture or animated GIF behind the interface, with its strength and
blur under your control.

Installing several mods shows a screen listing them, each one moving from
waiting to downloading to installed, rather than a button that says
"Installing..." for a minute. The Minecraft rows are larger and higher
contrast, and Play together is now one question with three answers instead of
three stacked panels.

One tunnel for the whole app. Pressing Invite while a tunnel was still
starting used to launch a second one and orphan the first, so there was more
than one address in play.

Show on Discord what you are playing, through Nyxen. Needs a one-minute
Discord application of your own - Discord takes the name from it - and the
Application ID is public, not a secret.

A volume slider for the room's music, with mute - and the music now ducks
while somebody is talking, so a call with music playing is actually usable.
The queue shows real track names instead of links, with the time.

Creating an account works. Sign up and sign in had their roles crossed:
creating an account reported that the account did not exist, and signing in
reported that the name was taken.

Minecraft: both Install buttons work, memory and Java can be set per
instance, sharing a modpack finds the groups you are in, and a modpack a
friend shares can be reviewed and installed.

Notifications. A message, a friend request, somebody accepting one, a message
in a room or a modpack shared with it now says so - and clicking it takes you
there. They wait if the window is behind a game instead of expiring unseen.

Calls: somebody whose connection drops is held as "reconnecting" instead of
vanishing, the "one connection failed" warning only appears while something
is genuinely wrong, and the DJ can be in any call. A shared screen has a full
screen button and is sent at a bitrate an ordinary upload can carry.

You stay online while Nyxen is open, even behind a full-screen game.

Setup opens straight away, and only one of it. A click used to produce
nothing for up to fifteen seconds while the installer unpacked itself, so
people clicked again - and again - until twenty copies were running. It now
shows a splash immediately, reaches its own window in about a second and a
half, and a second copy brings the first one to the front instead of starting
another.

Room music plays. The queue was in step on the server while the window
refused to start audio nothing had clicked on, so nobody heard anything.

Achievements without a Steam API key. Nyxen reads your achievements from your
own Steam profile page, so there is no key to create and nothing to paste - it
offers the accounts Steam has already signed in on your PC and you pick one. A
key stays optional and buys only two things: games you own but have not
installed, and reading a profile that is not public.

Updates inside the app. It checks for a new version, tells you what changed,
and installs it with one button. The download is checked against its published
SHA-256 before anything is run.

Setup can repair or remove. Running the installer when Nyxen is already
installed now offers Repair and Uninstall instead of silently reinstalling, and
the window itself has been rebuilt.

Rooms work. Opening a room used to load it into a hidden pane, which made Join
voice and the room's shared modpacks unreachable. Voice also shows who is
talking, with an icon when somebody is muted or not listening, and the DJ has
to be in the call to play music.

Choose your microphone and your headphones - in Settings, and in the call
itself, where you notice you picked the wrong one. Changing either takes effect
immediately without dropping the call.

Invite links can be pasted at any time. There is now one "Use an invite link"
box, reachable from Social and from Settings as well as the sign-in screen, so
a link that arrives after you already have an account is not a dead end - and
you can switch back to your own server just as easily.

Letting a friend in is one button. Nyxen opens the tunnel itself - no terminal
window, no port forwarding, no router settings - and the invite carries the
address, so the person you send it to does not have to type anything either.
